author: VijayabaskarR-06
title: ARM64 cross-compilation build fails with cc1plus: not a PCH file (invalid-pch) in openvino_reference
signature: cc1plus error cmake_pch hxx gch not a pch file werror invalid pch|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Build / Build
failed_jobs.symptom: CMake configure, build and install - OpenVINO JS API step fails: cc1plus reports cmake_pch.hxx.gch is not a PCH file and -Werror=invalid-pch turns it into a build error.

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation
failed_jobs.symptom: Aggregate status check fails because the upstream Build job failed.

key_errors: cc1plus: error: /__w/openvino/openvino/openvino/openvino_build/src/core/reference/CMakeFiles/openvino_reference.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch: not a PCH file [-Werror=invalid-pch]
cc1plus: all warnings being treated as errors
root_cause: This is a known recurring infrastructure issue (pattern 5b4b1e6917a69856, seen 13 times, 9 of them in the last 12 hours) on the ARM64 cross-compilation job. A second cmake re-configure/build invocation for the OpenVINO JS API package (`cmake -UTBB* ... -DCPACK_GENERATOR=NPM -DENABLE_SYSTEM_TBB=OFF -DENABLE_WHEEL=OFF`) re-uses the same BUILD_DIR as the primary build and re-triggers compilation of openvino_reference sources. Because the precompiled header file cmake_pch.hxx.gch under that build directory was generated/partially invalidated by a stale or concurrently-written ninja build graph (sccache + a reconfigured cmake invocation touching the same binary dir), gcc on the ARM64 cross-compile toolchain rejects it as 'not a PCH file', and -Werror=invalid-pch escalates the warning to a hard build failure. This is unrelated to the PR's actual source change (src/plugins/intel_cpu/src/nodes/matmul.cpp) which is never referenced in the failing compile unit (src/core/reference/src/op/einsum.cpp).
reproduction_steps: Not reliably reproducible locally — it depends on stale/corrupted PCH artifacts left over from a prior cmake re-configuration against the same build directory. To approximate: run the two-stage CMake sequence used by ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation (primary release build with ENABLE_FASTER_BUILD=ON/PCH enabled, followed by the `-UTBB* -DCPACK_GENERATOR=NPM` re-configure/build against the SAME BUILD_DIR) and attempt to recompile src/core/reference/src/op/einsum.cpp; the PCH mismatch surfaces intermittently.
recommended_actions: Use a separate BUILD_DIR (or clear/regenerate cmake_pch.hxx.gch) for the OpenVINO JS API re-configure step instead of reusing the primary release BUILD_DIR, so stale PCH objects from the first build cannot be picked up by the second ninja invocation.

Consider disabling ENABLE_FASTER_BUILD (PCH) specifically for the ARM64 cross-compile job, or set -DCMAKE_COMPILE_WARNING_AS_ERROR=OFF only around the JS API re-build stage, given this is a secondary packaging stage rather than primary validation.
Call remediate_transient_failure so the automated rerunner re-attempts the failed jobs — this has resolved prior occurrences of this exact pattern.

If this continues to recur at this frequency, escalate to the CI infra owners of ubuntu_22_arm64_cross_compilation.yml / job_build_linux.yml to fix the PCH reuse bug at the root (tracked via this pattern's recurring escalation).
prevention_strategies: Isolate the JS API npm-package CMake re-configure/build invocation into its own build directory (or force a clean of CMakeFiles/*.dir/cmake_pch.hxx.gch before the second ninja run) so precompiled headers generated for one CMake configuration are never reused by a subsequent, differently-configured build in the same directory. Add a CI guard that detects 'not a PCH file' and automatically retries once before failing the job.
historical_context: Identical failure recorded 13 times since 2026-09-24 (pattern 5b4b1e6917a69856), with 9 occurrences in the preceding 12 hours alone, affecting many unrelated PRs (#38601, #38559, #37717, #38261, #37908, #38604, #38607, #38611, #38030, #38483, and now #38407). This is a confirmed, long-standing flaky CI infrastructure defect in the ARM64 cross-compilation job's JS API build stage, not specific to this PR's code change.
